title: Rated power and active time
hook: A hypothetical load runs only one quarter of each hour. Should every hour use full power?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Use a stated duty fraction rather than treating rated power as continuous.

misconception: Every elapsed hour must be charged at full on-state power.
objective: Use a stated duty fraction rather than treating rated power as continuous.

claims.text: Illustrative power is 100W when on and 0W when off. A runs one quarter of the time; B continuously. Scaled model; illustrative:100W-on;0W-off;25%-or-100%;€0.30/kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Hours=8h, A=0.2kWh and B=0.8kWh. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",100,0.25,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",100,"x"],1000]; x denotes Hours. At x=8, A=0.2, B=0.8; recall at x=11: B=1.1. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: Multiply elapsed time by the on-time fraction before applying constant on-power. A nameplate-sized number cannot replace the duration actually spent at that power in this toy model.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",100,0.25,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",100,"x"],1000]; x denotes Hours. At x=8, A=0.2, B=0.8; recall at x=11: B=1.1. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Illustrative power is 100W when on and 0W when off. A runs one quarter of the time; B continuously. Change only Hours to 11h. What is B (Always-on) now? Correct: 1.1kWh. Use B's stated rule with Hours=11h: it gives 1.1kWh. Multiply elapsed time by the on-time fraction before applying constant on-power. A nameplate-sized number cannot replace the duration actually spent at that power in this toy model.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff.

recall.question: Illustrative power is 100W when on and 0W when off. A runs one quarter of the time; B continuously. Change only Hours to 11h. What is B (Always-on) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Hours=11h: it gives 1.1kWh. Multiply elapsed time by the on-time fraction before applying constant on-power. A nameplate-sized number cannot replace the duration actually spent at that power in this toy model.

safety.assumptions: Illustrative power is 100W when on and 0W when off. A runs one quarter of the time; B continuously.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
